recap_lines: A keyframe is a stored value, and interpolation computes the in-betweens.
Easing is the speed curve. Ease-in starts slow, and ease-out ends slow.
Timing is how long a move takes, and spacing is where its frames fall.
Anticipation is the wind-up, and squash and stretch shows speed and impact.
FK takes angles and gives the hand, and IK takes a target and gives angles.
A blend tree mixes clips by weight, and a state machine picks one clip.
bookends.command: Give me short cases from making a game, one at a time, each showing an animation problem or choice. Draw on keyframe, tween, ease-in, ease-out, timing, spacing, loop seam, anticipation, IK and root motion. I answer with the exact term and say why its look-alike does not fit. Wait for my answer before you reveal yours, then say whether I was right.
checks: Check: each case is about making a game, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and ruled out its look-alike.

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Newcomers often think an animation stores every frame of a move. It does not. A keyframe stores one value at one time, and the engine computes every frame in between. Animation is full of look-alike pairs like that one. This film goes through the terms group by group, each one shown, so you can name the exact one.

beats.narration_text: A plot of one value, position x, against time. A Keyframe is a value you store at a specific time. In this made-up example there are three, twenty at zero seconds, eighty at one second and fifty at two. Nothing is stored between them. For example, the sword's fast attack in Walker's finite state machine build stores a few rotation keys, the blade's angle at the start, at the top of the swing, and where it settles.

beats.narration_text: Interpolation is computing the values between the keys. Its results are the in-betweens, the open dots on the line. Only three keys are stored, and every other value is worked out when it is needed. At half a second it gives fifty. For example, between the sword's few stored angles, Godot computes the blade's angle on every frame of the swing, so nobody has to key each frame by hand.

beats.narration_text: A Tween is interpolation driven by code. It stores no keys. Code gives a start, an end and a duration, here x from zero to one hundred over one and a half seconds. For example, a health bar that glides to whatever the player's health is right now is a tween, because its end value comes from play, not from a file.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap. A keyframe is a stored value, and interpolation computes the in-betweens. Easing is the speed curve. Ease-in starts slow, and ease-out ends slow. Timing is how long a move takes, and spacing is where its frames fall. Anticipation is the wind-up, and squash and stretch shows speed and impact. FK takes angles and gives the hand, and IK takes a target and gives angles. A blend tree mixes clips by weight, and a state machine picks one clip.
